note: check: human and its approver; the push and the proposal as two separate permissions (BranchPush beside DestinationAdmission); destination.pushed as a ninth fact kind carrying the commit a pending decision is about, with destination.landed untouched so nothing recorded is reinterpreted; GET /v1/gates and the gate list. Fact vocabulary moves to 0.10.0 with it.

The answer path: POST /v1/flights/{ref}/decisions, DecisionRequest carrying the evidence manifest hash it was made against, DecisionRecorded carrying the re-evaluated admission, and DecisionObservations - what gg observed about how a decision was made, interpreted by nothing. PendingGate gains the manifest hash a decision is scoped to and the attempt count. All new types and new members; no enumeration that already crosses gained a value, so the fact vocabulary stays at 0.10.0.

Reject: DecisionOutcomes gains `rejected`, DecisionRequest gains the person's reason, and a lease carries LeaseFeedback - the sentence that sent an attempt back, attributed, marked as their words, and carrying nothing that could widen a move, a scope, an obligation, a destination or a budget. DiffBasis gains `prior-attempt` for a manifest measured from the previous attempt's head. And the fingerprints now hash closed vocabularies' VALUES: `rejected` and `prior-attempt` are both added values, and until this version neither ledger could see one. Fact vocabulary moves to 0.11.0 with it.

The second attempt's push: a lease repository reference gains `continuesFrom`, the commit a previous attempt pushed, so the runner is TOLD where to continue rather than inferring it from a branch anybody with push access can move - and so a manifest's prior-attempt basis and the commit it measures from cannot disagree. A flight summary gains `attempts`, counted from loops that ran rather than leases that were granted. Both are added members; no member moved and no value was added to a closed vocabulary.

The evidence payload. Obligation gains `evidence` - what a gate needs before anybody can answer it, declared in the envelope so the requirement is reviewed configuration rather than whatever the assembler had to hand, and an entry the flight cannot produce halts it rather than rendering a blank. Three new pinned types carry the case put to a person: GateEvidencePayload, GateEvidenceItem and EvidenceReference, the last with deliberately nowhere for a body to travel. Three new closed vocabularies with them: EvidenceItems, EvidenceDispositions - inline, digest, reference, and no fourth, so a shortened item is unrepresentable rather than merely unused - and EvidenceVoices, which marks a piece of evidence as measured or stated so an agent's words stay visibly different in kind from a verdict computed from facts. Also carries the vocabulary-membership attribute and its closure check; see fact-vocabulary 0.12.0 for why.

The write move and the environment's account of what bounds it. LoopMoves gains `write` - a VALUE in a closed enumeration, so it costs a fact-vocabulary bump to 0.13.0 and its ledger entry, and it is what finally lets a flight create a file. environment.identity gains moveEnforcement and movesProbed, behind a new MoveEnforcements vocabulary, so a fact set says how much this machine's executor actually bound and what was proven rather than assumed. LoopBudget gains attempts - flight-level, the reject-and-rerun cycle, and NOT the agent's internal turns, which are already called attempts on loop.outcome and would spend a budget of five on one loop thinking. A member, so it costs nothing and rides the value's bump.

Layers. ObligationProvenances gains `flight` and is declared ORDERED - it is a ranking, and ClosedVocabularies sorts a vocabulary's values unless told otherwise, so without this swapping org and flight would change which layer outranks which and move no fingerprint. That defect was found once already on the egress levels. No `team`: the design has three layers, this ships two, and a value nothing can produce is a value nobody maintains - its arrival is a version move and its absence is asserted. EnvelopeLayer and Composition carry a document with the layer BESIDE it rather than inside it, so a flight-level file cannot claim org. Composition is add-only rather than narrow-only: general widening detection over predicates is undecidable, and a lower layer adding its own while never touching a higher layer's has the same effect and a yes-or-no answer. Strengthening is adding, so there is no edit-a-higher-layer operation to secure. The parser now REFUSES a declared provenance and EnvelopeText.Render no longer emits one - what an author writes has no layer, and RenderComposed annotates the flattened form as a report that deliberately does not round-trip. A `when:` citing a verdict is refused by name, saying what breaks and naming the open question.

The envelope change as a FLIGHT. Two values in closed vocabularies, so both cost a version and every prior reader halts on them rather than guessing. ExecutorRungs gains `human` - a loop nothing automated runs - named rather than borrowing `frontier` with nobody listening, because a rung says what discharges the loop and recording an agent rung for work no agent does makes every later count of how much the machine did wrong in the flattering direction. It is a value in a Fact-fingerprinted vocabulary, so it also bumps fact-vocabulary to 0.14.0 with NO kind added; see that entry for why an envelope change produces no fact. DestinationKinds gains `envelope-change`, the first destination that is not somewhere code goes - which is what makes 'phase 2 arrives by adding a destination' a claim that can be tested rather than restated. And a new refusal: a loop at the human rung may declare no moves, because moves are bound by the executor a runner starts and this rung starts none, so a declared move would be granted by the envelope and enforced by nothing. That is the shape `write` was added to stop being, arriving through a different door. No member moved and no type was added.

A gate about something that is not a repository. PendingGate.Branch and .Commit stop being required and become nullable. This is the coupling that flying a flight with no repository actually found: every gate this contract could describe carried a branch and a commit, which was true of every gate that had ever existed - and made `flight` mean `agent run against a branch` in the one type a person reads when they are asked to answer for something. Null and never an empty string, because a gate carrying commit:"" makes 'no commit' and 'a commit nobody recorded' the same value, which is Article XI's failure with the fields swapped and the harder one to notice - the renderer prints a blank either way. The rule those members encoded is unchanged: a gate about work in a repository still waits for the push, because a decision about a tree on somebody's machine is a decision nobody can act on. That is now a rule about repository DESTINATIONS rather than a rule about gates. Two members loosened; nothing added, nothing removed, and no value added to a closed vocabulary - so the fact vocabulary does not move.

The verdict, closed on the wire. ObligationAttribution.Outcome was an unconstrained string while Attachments - in the same file, read off the same endpoint by the same client - was closed and fingerprinted. Three copies of `satisfied`/`violated` existed and none of them was here: the control plane's event vocabulary, a private pair inside the Engine whose own comment explains that two spellings of `violated` is a comparison failing silently in the permissive direction, and nothing at all on the boundary. So a value added to the verdict moved no ledger and asked nobody to think about it, which is the defect the vocabulary mechanism exists to close, sitting inside the mechanism's own file. It carries `unevaluable`, which nothing writes - a halted flight records no verdict at all, because a verdict set with a hole in it reads as a complete answer - and it is declared because the store can hold it and a wire vocabulary missing a value the writer can emit is the permissive silence one spelling away. It shares that word with Attachments and means something else by it: there the CONDITION could not be read, here the obligation applied and could not be MEASURED, and merging them would make 'this rule did not apply' and 'this rule could not be checked' one value. Closed now rather than earlier because good-grief:DecisionVisibilityTests first had to prove the value arrives on this surface - a spelling nobody checks against a behaviour nobody measures is not a guard. No member moved, no type was added, and the fact vocabulary does not move: a verdict is produced by the control plane, not by a runner.

ADR-0012 B2: the decision endpoint stops answering inline. POST /v1/flights/{ref}/decisions declares 202 with no body instead of 200 with a DecisionRecorded, because the write becomes a command and answering inline would mean the endpoint waiting for its own event to land - the blocking read the whole change removes. 409 survives and that is not an inconsistency: a decision made against work that has since moved is refused BEFORE anything is dispatched, from state the request already has, so what became asynchronous is the recording rather than the check on the way in. The client tolerates BOTH answers for now, which is what lets the two repositories land this in either order; when no control plane answers inline the 200 branch is dead and deleting it is a change with its own reason. THE SURFACE HASH IS UNCHANGED AND THAT IS A GAP, not an oversight in this entry: ContractSurfaceTests hashes pinned types, their members and closed vocabularies, and reaches ProtocolSurface.Endpoints not at all - so a route's path, method, audience, statuses and response type can all move without the version that describes the contract moving. This is the closed-vocabulary defect one layer up, and the same sentence applies: the guard that exists to force this conversation could not see the change that most needs one. The version is bumped by hand here BECAUSE the mechanism did not ask, and EndpointSurfaceTests now pins a fingerprint of the routes so the next one is at least loud. Folding that into the contract surface proper would move every recorded hash and belongs in a step about the mechanism.

Shipping facts is accepted rather than answered, and the landing decision moves to a route of its own. The control plane's evidence write becomes a command (ADR-0012), so POST /v1/leases/{id}/facts answers 202 and its body reports only what was refused before anything was written - validation, cleanliness, classification and budget are all decided from the request itself. Accepted and duplicates leave: both are answers only the write has, and duplicates especially, because dedupe moves into the projection where a repeated event is ignored rather than counted. Push and admission could not simply be dropped. LandAsync reads both and treats each as REFUSED when absent, which is correct while the answer arrives with the write and a silent bug the moment it does not: 'not evaluated yet' and 'no' become the same value, and a flight that was going to be admitted quietly never pushes. So they move to GET /v1/leases/{id}/admission, and LandingDecision carries `settled` - absence means refusal only once the question has been answered at all.

An invitation into an existing tenant. POST /v1/invitations answers with a URL and an expiry, and /v1/invitations joins the governed prefixes so the declaration closes over it - an invitation is the strongest capability the product issues, because whoever holds the link becomes a principal in somebody else's tenant, and an undeclared route under that prefix would be an unaudited way to make one. InvitationRequest is EMPTY and stays empty: an invitation names nobody. Carrying an address would imply the control plane delivers it, which it does not - the person who ran the verb does that, by whatever means they already trust - and carrying a tenant would let a caller name one rather than be one. InvitationIssued echoes a URL the control plane built, exactly as DeviceAuthorizationStarted echoes a verification URI: where the web surface lives is deployment knowledge, and a client that composed it from a base address would guess wrong the first time somebody deployed it anywhere but a laptop.

The claim becomes a request with a status. POST /v1/leases:claim answers 202 with a LeaseClaimAccepted - a request id and an interval - and GET /v1/leases/claims/{id} says what became of it. Both old answers go, and losing the 204 is the point rather than a side effect: an idle fleet and a fleet blocked on a credential nobody has registered were the SAME answer, so the only thing a runner could report was silence, identical to the silence of a system with nothing to do. That was tolerable while a claim could be decided from state the control plane already held; it stopped being tolerable when identity moved behind an announcement and 'the credential is not here yet' became a real state with nowhere to live. LeaseClaimStates is closed - pending, waiting, granted, expired - so a fifth costs a version and every prior reader halts rather than guessing, and `waiting` is the one that did not exist before. LeaseClaimStatus.Lease is absent unless the state is granted, which is LandingDecision.Settled's arrangement for LandingDecision.Settled's reason: absence has to mean one thing. pollAfterSeconds is server-supplied and load-bearing rather than a hint - the control plane holding the claim open WAS the rate limiter and the runner has no backoff of its own, so a cadence the runner invented would either hammer an endpoint that now answers instantly or idle past work that was ready; DeviceAuthorizationStarted.PollIntervalSeconds is the same arrangement for the same reason. LeaseGranted gains unresolvedRepos, which fixes a silent failure older than this change: an empty `credentials` was two facts - no credential registered, or one not yet known to this control plane - and the runner's TryGetValue result was never consulted, so a repository with neither fetched ANONYMOUSLY. A public one succeeded and a private one failed later at git's own words with nothing pointing at the cause. Naming them turns that into a refusal before anything is materialized, which is what the push path has always done. The consequence is deliberate: a public repository with no registered credential is now refused rather than cloned anonymously, because absence cannot keep meaning both 'needs none' and 'nobody registered one' - that ambiguity IS the bug. A member on LeaseGranted, three new types, and one new closed vocabulary; the fact vocabulary does not move, because none of this is something a runner reports.

The seed becomes a wire resource, served at GET /v1/flights/{ref}/seed. TakeSeed, TakeMeasurements and TakeSeedComposer move out of Gg.Client and into this package, because the control plane composes the seed now and the two repositories cannot reference each other - only this package crosses. The composer moves WITH the types deliberately: reimplementing the composition on the other side would be two derivations of one document and they would drift on the first change to either, which is the same argument CredentialLocator.ForRepo is here for. TakeSeed.TreePath is GONE, and its absence is the point of the change. It said 'where the work is, on this machine', and that one member is why a stopped flight was resumable by whoever sat at that keyboard and by nobody else. Git already moves a working tree between machines; what git cannot reconstruct is what was tried and ruled out, and that is what a seed is. LoopDigest.Validate already refused an absolute path for exactly this reason - 'a digest carries paths a person can compare across flights, not paths on one machine' - so the fact was designed portable while the feature was built local. In its place: a transcript reference and a state that SAYS where it is. A transcript holds the customer's own code and never crosses, and ArtifactScopes has exactly one value, so what a person on the far side of a handoff gets is a hash and a locator they cannot follow. TranscriptStates is closed with two values - elsewhere, none - and there is no `present` because the platform cannot produce one; declaring a state nothing reaches would be a promise it does not keep. The two read differently on purpose: an absent section and an artifact that does not exist send a person to different places, which is the same rule the account's NO ACCOUNT line already follows. AccountState stops being a C# enum and becomes AccountStates, a closed string vocabulary. An enum crossing this boundary serializes as an INTEGER: unreadable to the auditor this package exists for, and invisible to the mechanism that discovers closed vocabularies by shape and forces a version when one gains a value. It was only ever an enum because the seed was a document one console composed for itself. And the seed carries a revision of its own. A second number beside the protocol revision, which earns itself: the protocol revision says which conversation the two sides are having, and this says what shape a document an AGENT reads as declared context is in. A shape that changed silently would change what every future resumption knows with nothing anywhere to point at. Two pinned types, two closed vocabularies, one route. The fact vocabulary does not move: a seed is composed FROM facts and is not one, and nothing a runner reports changed shape.

A takeover becomes a HOLD, and this is the first entry in this ledger that REMOVES a route. POST /v1/flights/{id}/takeover is gone and three replace it: takeover:claim, takeover:renew, takeover:return. What went wrong with the old one is when it was written. It took a TakeoverRecord carrying heldForMs - how long somebody held the flight - so it was posted once they had already finished. That is a record, not a hold: two people on two machines both see a takeable flight, both take it, and both find out afterwards. Nothing about it was atomic, because it was never asking for anything. Correctness here needs a claim, which is the same answer the lease and the device code already have - and the direction this fails in is the dangerous one. A read model lagging over a permission table fails EMPTY, which is a liveness problem; lagging over a HOLD fails permissive, and the second claimant takes a flight somebody is working. Deleted rather than deprecated beside the claim. It was reachable only through a client method nothing in the product called, because nothing in the product ever took a flight over - unreleased in effect - and a route that records a takeover without holding anything, sitting next to the claim that replaces it, is a shape somebody will build against. TakeoverRecord goes with it, for the same reason: a wire type no route carries is a type somebody will find and use. The claim answers 409 with TakeoverHeld, and that refusal is the product rather than an error path. 'Somebody else has this' sends a person nowhere; a name and two instants tell them whether to wait, to ask, or to come back. It is also the only thing standing between a portable handoff and two people confidently editing divergent copies of one flight, each believing they hold it. The renewal exists because a hold has to expire on a CLOCK. Attendance lapses - somebody closes their laptop - and judging whether a person is still at their desk is exactly what ADR-0005 refuses. So the hold has a window, the holder renews it while they are working, and renewWithinSeconds is the server's number rather than the client's: a cadence a client invents is wrong on one of the two machines this feature exists to span, and DeviceAuthorizationStarted.PollIntervalSeconds is the precedent. The generation is the fence, exactly as it is on a lease: a holder whose hold lapsed and whose flight was then claimed by somebody else is told so rather than handed it back. There are TWO return types now and the split is about who writes each. TakeoverReturn stays as it is: a file a person writes by hand, naming the flight, because a file left over from a previous takeover parses perfectly and describes a different flight and applying it would put one flight's decision onto another. It cannot carry a generation because nobody types one. TakeoverReturnRequest is what gg posts - the flight is in the path, and the generation is what stops a decision landing on a hold that has since moved. What it deliberately does NOT carry is how long the flight was held: the control plane knows when the hold was claimed and what time it is, and a duration supplied by the party it is about is not a measurement. Five pinned types added, one removed, one route removed and three added. The fact vocabulary does not move: a hold is not something a runner reports, and no fact changed shape.

The envelope decides whether work that was NOT admitted may still reach the forge. Destination gains preserve-unadmitted, DestinationPushed gains preserved, and DestinationBranch gains ForHandoff. Why it is needed: a flight that halted, violated or exhausted has no branch anywhere. HandoffRoot's own comment names it - 'a landed flight has a branch and a proposal, a violated or exhausted one has neither, and the work exists only here, which is precisely the flight somebody wants to take over'. So the one flight most likely to need taking over is the one that cannot be taken over from another machine, because its work is on a disk. Why it is a permission rather than a behaviour: inverting that is not free. Unadmitted work would exist on the customer's remote, and a violated flight's code reaching the forge is a governance question rather than a plumbing one. AdmissionEngine.Preserve already refuses to ASK A PERSON about work that failed a machine check, and the same argument does not automatically extend to PRESERVING it - so the envelope says, rather than the platform deciding. ABSENCE MEANS NO, and that is the load-bearing half. The failure mode is a tenant discovering that every abandoned agent attempt is a branch on their default remote, so an envelope that does not name this pushes nothing - which is also exactly what every envelope written before 0.41.0 continues to mean. Article XI, and the same reason an unknown predicate halts rather than evaluating false. Null and false are one answer and there is no third state a reader could take for yes. A MEMBER RATHER THAN A VALUE, so no reader has to halt: a member may be added freely and a value in a closed enumeration may not. That is why this costs a contract version and no vocabulary. It is refused on a destination that is not a pull-request. An envelope-change destination has no branch and no repository, so the permission names nothing there - and a knob that silently does nothing on one kind of destination is one somebody sets and believes they granted. The text form writes it only when it is declared. Emitting preserve-unadmitted: false for every destination that omits it would rewrite every tenant's document on the next `envelope show`, and a diff nobody made is how a review practice gets abandoned. The parser reads only 'true' and 'false' - YAML dialects accept yes, on and y as truth, and a governance permission whose meaning depends on which parser opened the file is not a permission. ForHandoff is a second branch name because it is a second fact: gg/handoff/GG-42 rather than gg/GG-42, so a flight preserved for handoff and the same flight later admitted cannot fight over one ref - the second push would either be refused as an existing branch or would overwrite the work somebody was about to take over. It stays under the gg/ prefix so whatever cleans up this platform's branches still recognises it. DestinationPushed.preserved moves the FACT vocabulary as well, to 0.15.0: a gg/ branch with no pull request is not a proposal, and a reader counting branches has to be able to tell work that was admitted from work that was merely kept.

An exhausted loop can hand its work to another loop. ExhaustionPolicies gains handoff-to-agent and LeaseLoop gains resumesFrom. A VALUE in a closed enumeration, which is a break rather than an addition: the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt, so every prior reader meeting handoff-to-agent stops rather than guessing what to do when a budget runs out. That is the behaviour and not a defect. Existing envelopes are unchanged in meaning, because none of them named it - handoff-to-human still parses, still validates, still renders identically, and still means a person is asked. It needs no new machinery, because `executor` is already a parameter of a loop: an agent resuming another agent's work is the same loop starting again on a rung, with the seed as declared context. What was missing was somewhere for on-exhaustion to point. It is bounded by LoopBudget.Attempts and by nothing else. That field already counts how many times a flight's loop may run; without it this value would be an instruction to retry for ever, which is a termination condition nobody agreed to. LeaseLoop.resumesFrom is the load-bearing half and the reason it is a member on the LEASE rather than a route: GET /v1/flights/{ref}/seed answers a DEVELOPER session, deliberately, because a runner able to call it could read what every flight in the tenant tried and ruled out from a credential meant only to let it hold one lease. So a resuming loop is handed its context on the lease it already has, which is also the shape ContextBinding has. It carries the RENDERED seed rather than the model: it reaches an executor as declared context beside the intent, and rendering it runner-side would be a second implementation of a document this package already renders once. Absent on a first attempt, which is the ordinary case - there is nothing to resume from. A member that had to be present would make every lease carry an empty document, so 'no prior attempt' and 'a prior attempt that measured nothing' would read the same. Nothing in it is customer content: it is composed from facts that already crossed, and TakeSeed carries no absolute path and no machine name by construction - the transcript is named and never included. The fact vocabulary does not move. An on-exhaustion policy is read off an envelope and a lease is not a fact, so neither is something a runner reports.

The envelope learns to ask for an environment, and the fleet learns to answer. Two SELECTIONS arrive on the envelope - environment and repository - as optional members, which is the free kind of change: every prior document parses, validates, renders identically, and means what it meant. A selection is deliberately not a bound: every other envelope field composes across layers through a merge operator, these get none, because two layers naming different environments is not an empty intersection, it is a mistake, and the composer refuses it rather than merging it. Declared once, validated for MEMBERSHIP at apply against the tenant's chart, never merged. The contract owns only the shape (one line, non-blank, absent-stays-absent); membership is the control plane's question because the control plane has the chart. Re-applying an existing envelope under this version mints a new envelope version - the ADR-0013 hazard - and that is a decision, not an accident: the fields land in today's flat envelope now and migrate into role-shaped types when the named-envelope ADR lands, two minting events budgeted with eyes open. The chart itself crosses the wire as ChartEnvironmentRequest / EnvironmentCharted / EnvironmentChart under a NEW governed prefix /v1/environments: the chart decides what an envelope may say and what a fleet must satisfy, so an undeclared route under it would be an unaudited way to widen every envelope - the same argument /v1/credentials came in on. A chart entry's meaning is optional and its absence IS the disposition: LabelDispositions (measured | stated) arrives as its OWN closed vocabulary rather than reusing EvidenceVoices, though the words coincide today, because one says what a gate's evidence is and the other what a capability claim is, and coupling two closed enumerations makes a value added for either a halt for readers of the other. AdvertisedLabel carries the word beside the name and RunnerSummary gains labels, so a stated claim can never be read as a measurement by losing its qualifier in transit. The checklist - Checklist and ChecklistItem, served at GET /v1/envelope/plan (tenant-level: what WOULD a flight need) and GET /v1/flights/{ref}/checklist (pinned to what that flight compiled) - is the third flight artifact: the plan says what would happen, the log says what happened, the checklist says what must hold first. Its satisfier vocabulary is CLOSED at two values, already-true-via-matching and nobody-declared-capability-gap, and the closure is the design: a third value means a strategy exists, which is a design event that arrives as a deliberate contract change, not a string. FlightSummary gains requiredLabels and waiting - refusal at apply, waiting at flight: apply has an actor at the keyboard to inform, a queued flight has nobody, so it waits loudly with the sentence on the one document gg flights, gg show and --json all read. Null means not waiting, the LeaseClaimStatus.Lease absence rule. All members and new types; the only closed vocabularies added are new ones, so nothing any prior reader knew changed meaning.
